articles.title: TANUVAS invites applications for UG courses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Tanuvas) has opened its application portal for undergraduate courses, including Bachelor's in Veterinary Sciences and Animal Husbandry, and various B. Tech programs. Applications are open from 10 a.m. on May 25 to 5 p.m. on June 17 through the university's website: https://adm.tanuvas.ac.in.  Candidates can find details regarding seat reservations for NRIs, NRI-sponsored candidates, and foreign nationals on the portal.

articles.title: Innovation begins with understanding the fundamentals: Prakash Balasubramanian - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prakash Balasubramanian, senior director at Infineon Technologies, emphasized the importance of foundational knowledge for technological breakthroughs during the inauguration of "Nirmaan Utsav" in Kalaburagi city. He highlighted the evolution of technologies over decades and urged students to think innovatively. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Shaloo encouraged students to combine academic learning with practical experience and stay updated on emerging fields like drones, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity. HKE Society president and MLC Shashil Namoshi noted that PDA Engineering College is nurturing future-ready students through events like "Nirmaan Utsav."

articles.title: Conference on higher education held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jebi Mather, MP, emphasized the need for continuous modernization of Kerala's higher education sector during a conference on 'Higher Education Reforms'.  Prof. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor of Cochin University of Science and Technology, highlighted the importance of developing employability skills alongside academic achievements. The conference, organized by Kerala Principals’ Council, featured sessions led by prominent figures in academia and literature.

articles.title: Four from Telangana State colleges to go on Sakura Science Programme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four students from Telangana have been selected to participate in the Japan Science and Technology Agency’s (JST) SAKURA Science Programme. The seven-day program, starting May 24th, will allow the students to visit advanced scientific institutions, interact with scientists, and gain exposure to Japan's innovation in education and science. The students were selected through district-level nominations and a state-level screening test conducted earlier this year.

articles.title: Turkiye shutters liberal Istanbul university seized in criminal probe | Education News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan revoked the operating license for Istanbul Bilgi University, a private university known for its liberal values, citing insufficient education standards. The closure, effective immediately, follows a criminal investigation into the institution's parent company and has sparked protests from students who will now continue their studies at Mimar Sinan University. The Council of Higher Education promised to ensure student safety during this transition.

articles.title: Over 2.3 lakh students register for TNEA 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 2.34 lakh candidates have registered for the Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA) 2026 portal, with many completing application and fee payment processes. The registration deadline is June 2nd, followed by certificate uploads until June 6th.  Random number assignments will occur on June 5th, with certificate verification starting June 8th and a rank list published on June 29th. Counselling for special category students, including those in the eminent sportspersons category, is expected to begin in July after Class XII results are released.

articles.title: Minority commission recommends upgrading Pallikkal govt. school in Wayanad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala State Commission for Minorities recommended that the Pallikkal Government Lower Primary (LP) School in Wayanad be upgraded to an upper primary (UP) school during the 2026-27 academic year. The recommendation was made following a petition submitted by the school's management and favorable response from the Wayanad Deputy Director of Education, who acknowledged the school's facilities and student population.  The school has all necessary infrastructure for an UP section, including smart classrooms and additional construction under the Wayanad Package.

articles.title: NCERT book row: SC modifies earlier order concerning 3 academics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court on Friday reversed its March 11 order that directed the Centre, States, and others to disassociate from three academics involved in a controversial chapter of the NCERT's Class 8 social science textbook. The court left it up to the Centre, states, universities, and institutions to make their own decisions regarding the issue without being influenced by its previous observations.  The Court also clarified that its comments were made in context of the content and not the individuals involved.

articles.title: VIT-A.P. University celebrates ninth anniversary at Amaravati campus - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: HCLTech Head of Campus Relations Director Prasath P. emphasized the importance of industry-academia collaboration during his speech at the 9th University Day celebrations at VIT-A.P. University. He commended the university's efforts in research, entrepreneurship, and community service, stating that graduates from such institutions are well-prepared for the global workforce.

articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged States to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

articles.title: Lakshmi could have been a child bride - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lakshmi, a 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh, wrote a song expressing her desire to continue her education and resist early marriage. Her father initially dismissed the message but was persuaded by anganwadi workers and village pradhan.  The village now features painted messages advocating for change in response to Lakshmi's powerful lyrics.

articles.title: IT-based skill training launched for inmates at Visakhapatnam Central Jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Prisons Department and the Skill Development Institute (SDI), Visakhapatnam, launched an IT-based skill development course for inmates at the Visakhapatnam Central Jail. The "Office Assistant" program, inaugurated by Visakhapatnam District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, aims to equip inmates with industry-oriented skills and improve their employability prospects after release.  The two-month course covers computer applications, office administration, digital communication, and employability skills, with successful participants receiving a certification from SDI Visakhapatnam.

articles.title: Charges dismissed against official at school where 6-year-old shot teacher
articles.rephrased_article: Ebony Parker, former assistant principal at a Virginia elementary school, has been cleared of all charges against her stemming from the shooting incident in January 2023. Judge Rebecca Robinson dismissed eight felony counts, including disregard for life, after the defense argued that the state had not presented sufficient evidence to prove their case. The six-year-old student who fired a single shot at teacher Abigail Zwerner, who suffered injuries requiring surgery, is being cared for by his mother, Deja Taylor.

articles.title: Russia’s Sechenov University assigns ‘Visiting Professor’ status to Basappa Salundi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sechenov First Moscow State Medical (SMSM) University in Russia has appointed Basappa Salundi, chairman of the Department of Organic Chemistry at the University of Mysore, as a 'Visiting Professor'. This honorary title, established in 2025, does not involve formal employment or salary and is awarded to recognized external specialists. The university hopes this will enhance its prestige and competitiveness by attracting leading scientists who can facilitate increased publications and international grants.

articles.title: After State-run schools, Vande Mataram now compulsory in all Bengal madrasas - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education has mandated the singing of "Vande Mataram" during assembly prayers in all government, aided, and recognized madrasas across the state. The order, issued by the Director of Madrasa Education, states that this is effective immediately and supersedes previous practices.  This decision follows a similar mandate for state-run schools announced earlier in May.

articles.title: I tried to buy a Cambridge paper online, this is what happened - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: This summer, leaked Cambridge International Examinations (CAIE) papers have caused widespread disruption for Pakistani students.  Cambridge Assessment International Education (CAIE) reported the theft and unauthorized sharing of examination papers on May 7th and 14th, with evidence being sent to platforms where the leaks circulated. The agency is investigating both incidents thoroughly through digital forensics, analysis of online platforms, and cooperation with law enforcement. Anant Nanda, an A Level student from Lahore, discovered a Discord server called "Cambridge Leaks" that sells leaked papers for $100 each.  He attempted to purchase a Mathematics Paper 1 exam paper, which was available on the website for sale. The CAIE has assured students and schools that it is working to protect them from this problem. Parents are concerned about fair assessments and the future of their children's education.

articles.title: Doctor can’t enrol as advocate without cancelling registration: HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court ruled that a registered medical practitioner cannot be enrolled as an advocate, unless she cancels her homeopathic license. The court cited the Bar Council of Kerala (BCK)'s duty to ensure applicants are not engaged in other professions and the Kerala State Medical Practitioners Act, 2021, which prohibits practicing medicine alongside another profession.  The court upheld the BCK's decision to deny the petitioner's enrollment application.

articles.title: TGBCESDTC to conduct 4-day AI and life skills training programme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana BC Employability Skill Development and Training Centre (TGBCESDTC), in collaboration with the Magic Bus India Foundation, will host a four-day interactive workshop from May 21 to June 11 across various districts of Telangana. The program aims to introduce district-level youth to artificial intelligence technologies and enhance their employability skills.  Interested youth are advised to contact their nearest TGBCESDTC centers for enrollment and further information.

articles.title: NCC annual training camp begins - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The NCC Group Training Centre, West Hill, hosted the annual training camp for 380 cadets from Kozhikode, Kannur, and Palakkad districts.  The ten-day program, led by Col. Venkatesan R., Commanding Officer of the NCC 9 Kerala Girls Battalion, aims to foster civic sense and social responsibility in participants through classes on personality development, health and hygiene, self-defense, and NCC subject training. The camp concludes on May 22nd.

articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

articles.title: Students get clarity on career choices at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling Fair in Mysuru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students attending the Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling Fair-2026 at Vidya Vardhaka College of Engineering in Mysuru sought guidance on their future career paths.  Experts from various fields provided information and advice to over 500 students, many accompanied by their parents, helping them navigate available career options based on individual interests and aptitudes.

articles.title: Why Robert F. Smith’s Morehouse surprise donation mattered even more after graduation day
articles.rephrased_article: Robert F. Smith, an entrepreneur, made a significant donation of $34 million to Morehouse College in 2019, covering the student debt for the graduating class and that of their parents. The gesture resonated widely due to its impact on both students' immediate financial burdens and the broader issue of educational debt in African-American communities.  This event highlighted the significant role family debt plays in college expenses and sparked a conversation about educational equality and financial empowerment within historically black colleges and universities (HBCUs).

articles.title: Results show it is possible to raise quality without failing students: Sivankutty - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Sivankutty, former Minister for General Education, congratulated students on the high pass percentage of 99.07 in the State syllabus Class X exams. He acknowledged the hard work and dedication of students and their families, emphasizing that this was not the end but a new beginning. Sivankutty also highlighted the changes in question paper pattern aimed at preparing students for national-level entrance tests, stating that these adjustments did not negatively impact student performance.

articles.title: Tennessee school district bans Alex Haley’s Roots under 2022 state law | Tennessee | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Knox County Schools (KCS) in Tennessee have removed the novel "Roots" from school library shelves due to a state law requiring review of materials for appropriateness. The decision, made under the Age-Appropriate Materials Act, follows a review by KCS's book-banning committee which deemed an excerpt not age-appropriate.  The author's grandson and advocates for free expression criticize the ban as short-sighted and harmful to students' understanding of history.

articles.title: The $55 million blueprint: How New York’s busiest library swapped worn-out shelves for a civic living room
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Public Library received a $55 million donation from the Stavros Niarchos Foundation to renovate its Mid-Manhattan branch, which had become outdated due to high usage. The renovation transformed the library into a modern hub for learning, interaction, and professional development with features like open spaces, learning zones, and an outdoor terrace.  The redesigned space saw significant increases in visits and circulation numbers, demonstrating the potential of public libraries as democratic resources for everyday citizens.

articles.title: Three-day Mohiniyattam masterclass at Fort Kochi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Kalamandalam, a performance arts institution, is hosting a three-day masterclass on Mohiniyattam from May 22 to 24. The event, part of the Kalamandalam's Masterclass series, will be led by artiste Methil Devika.  Participants must have at least five years of experience in an Indian classical dance form and apply online before May 19th. For more information visit www.kalamandalam.ac.in or call 98471 88288.

articles.title: US justice department accuses Yale medical school of illegally using race in admissions | Yale University | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice accused Yale University of illegally considering race in admissions to its medical school, alleging that Black and Hispanic students have a significantly higher chance of admission than white or Asian students despite lower academic credentials. Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon stated that the department is seeking a voluntary resolution agreement with the university but has the authority to take legal action if necessary. This follows a similar accusation against the University of California, Los Angeles, and aligns with the Trump administration's efforts to restrict race-based admissions policies.

articles.title: Govt orders inquiry into Cambridge exam leaks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The interior ministry directed the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to investigate the alleged leak of Cambridge International Education (CIE) exam papers, in coordination with CIE. The investigation was prompted by a meeting chaired by Interior Secretary Muhammad Khurram Agha, where concerns were raised about the second suspected leak of an O Level Mathematics paper and the potential theft of exam materials. The British deputy high commissioner stated that the matter appeared to involve theft rather than a true leak, while CIE representatives assured the forum that they maintain strict standards for examination integrity. The meeting also saw discussions on strengthening CIE's system capacity to address weaknesses in the examination process and ensuring transparency.

articles.title: SRMIST, The Hindu to organise webinar on c - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), in partnership with The Hindu, is hosting a webinar titled "Career Beyond the Obvious: Unlocking New Pathways in Humanities and Sciences." The event will feature experts from various fields discussing how skills in humanities and sciences are opening doors to careers in research, technology, media, analytics, and more. Panelists include A. Vinay Kumar, Dean of Faculty of Sciences and Humanities at SRMIST, Deepa Sethi, Executive Chair of Globe, IIM Kozhikode, and Kamal Karanth, Co-founder of Xpheno Private Limited.  The webinar is part of the Future Career Conversations series and will be hosted by Prince Frederick of The Hindu.

articles.title: NEET-UG, 2026 paper leak: Experts call for reforms in exam process, exemption of State-government seats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors’ Association for Social Equality (DASE) general secretary G.R. Ravindranath and Indian Medical Association (IMA) former president Rajeev Jayadevan have called for compulsory registration of all medical entrance exam coaching centers, a computerised NEET exam, and exemption of state-government controlled medical seats from the single-window national system to prevent malpractices in the exam.  They also suggested free coaching centers with boarding facilities for poor students and the use of technology like encrypted questions and multi-session testing to ensure a fair and merit-based process.

articles.title: ‘Limited’ religious symbols to be allowed with uniforms in Karnataka schools and colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government withdrew its 2022 order requiring prescribed uniforms in educational institutions and replaced it with a new order allowing students to wear “limited” traditional and faith-based symbols alongside their uniforms.  Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa stated that the decision aims to promote secular values and equal respect for all religions and traditions within schools, while maintaining institutional discipline.

articles.title: NSUI holds protest outside Education Minister’s residence over NEET paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) protested outside Dharmendra Pradhan's residence in Delhi, demanding his resignation following allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The protesters accused the Education Minister of failing to protect students and demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the incident, along with action against those involved. The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the exam and announced it would be retaken at a later date.

articles.title: The south London community where ‘pioneering’ scholarship choristers are made | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: St John the Divine, Kennington (SJDK), a church in south London, has produced several young choristers who have secured scholarships to prestigious music institutions.  The church's youth choral program, which began in 2013, aims to remove barriers that keep working-class children from classical music. The program provides transportation and snacks for rehearsals, making it accessible for families with limited resources. Ed Picton-Turbervill, an award-winning composer and organist, credits the program's success in fostering musical talent and breaking down racial prejudice within the community.  N’raeah, a four-year-old chorister from south London, has been accepted into St Paul's Cathedral school, a testament to the impact of the program.

articles.title: Good show by Ernakulam schools in Class 12 exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Schools under the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in Ernakulam district achieved high pass rates in Class 12 examinations.  Bhavan’s Vidya Mandir, Elamakkara, and Rajagiri Public School, Kalamassery led with the highest number of distinctions, exceeding 100 students each. Several schools recorded 100% pass rates, including Sacred Heart CMI Public School, Thevara and Mar Thoma Public School, Thengode.

articles.title: Cambridge confirms leak of AS-level Mathematics paper, postpones upcoming exam as 'precautionary step' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) confirmed the leak of an AS-level Mathematics exam paper on May 12th and postponed another exam scheduled for Friday, May 15th.  The board is investigating the incident and working to understand the extent of the leak. Uzma Yousuf, Country Director of Pakistan, stated that the board's decisions were made by experienced professionals who prioritize fairness and reliability in grading. She emphasized that leaks are rare and stressed the importance of trusting official statements from CIE. The release date for AS- and A-Level results remains unchanged (August 11th).

articles.title: Cancellation sparks anger, anxiety among aspirants in Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NEET (UG) 2026 has been canceled following allegations of a paper leak, causing widespread frustration and anxiety among students, parents, and educators in Telangana.  Long-term aspirants like Mounika U. expressed disappointment over the system failure, while G. Vijay Kumar, a NEET trainer, highlighted the emotional impact on young students. The Students’ Federation of India (Telangana) criticized the government's handling of the situation, calling it an "administrative failure." Protests are planned by student groups and organizations demanding fair and transparent examination processes.

articles.title: The $1.8 billion pivot: How Michael Bloomberg’s historic gift rewrote the rules of college access | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Bloomberg donated $1.8 billion to Johns Hopkins University, the largest donation in American history, to fund undergraduate scholarships and eliminate financial barriers for prospective students. This move aims to address a psychological obstacle preventing talented individuals from low-income backgrounds from pursuing higher education due to high tuition fees. The endowment will ensure that all accepted students can attend without incurring debt, fostering an environment where merit is prioritized over wealth.  This historic gift signifies a shift in the focus of philanthropy towards creating opportunities for excellence and dismantling financial barriers in higher education.

articles.title: School education index: Kerala betters grade, score - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Despite the denial of funds by the Union government, Kerala has improved its performance in the Union Ministry of Education’s Performance Grading Index 2.0 for States/Union Territories (UT) for the year 2024-25. The state received a Prachesta-2 grade, an improvement from Prachesta-3 in 2023-24, with scores rising from 594.2 to 687.7.  Kerala achieved the topmost Utkarsh grade (72.8-80) in access and the Uttam-1 grade (81-90.9) in teacher education and training, among other achievements. The report highlights Kerala's progress despite challenges, including a lack of funding from the Union government.

articles.title: What you need to know about Karnataka’s Rohith Vemula Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has approved the revised Rohith Vemula Bill, 2026. The bill aims to prevent discrimination and injustice for students, faculty, and staff from scheduled castes and tribes (SC/ST) by guaranteeing equal access to education in all higher educational institutions across the state.

articles.title: NEET-UG examination 2026: One suspect arrested from Nashik - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG examination for 2026 after an alleged paper leak, leading to the arrest of a suspect in Maharashtra. The Rajasthan Police requested the Maharashtra police to detain the individual who was apprehended after changing his appearance.  The cancellation has drawn criticism from opposition leaders, including Rohit Pawar, who pointed out that the state government's new law against paper leaks is insufficient and called for stricter action against those involved. A CBI inquiry into the matter has been initiated.

articles.title: PMDC says medical students must qualify for MDCAT, obtain registration before going abroad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) announced new regulations for students pursuing medical or dental education abroad. The PMDC stated that all students must qualify for the MDCAT examination, obtain registration with the council, and verify the foreign institution's accreditation by either the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME) or the World Directory of Medical Schools.  The PMDC emphasized the importance of ensuring a minimum of 6,200 hours of education, at least 80% attendance over five years, language proficiency in English or local languages, and passing the National Registration Examination for registration in Pakistan upon completion. The PMDC also directed students to provide complete details of their residence and contact information before departure, as well as secure a multiple-entry visa valid for the duration of their studies.

articles.title: Cambridge AS-level Mathematics paper allegedly leaked, students claim - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE), part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, is facing accusations of paper leaks for the AS-level Mathematics exam in Karachi. Students allege that the Tuesday's exam was identical to a solved paper they saw on social media.  CIE states that it investigates all allegations of paper leaks but does not comment on individual reports. The organization has offered resits for candidates impacted by previous leaks and is currently investigating this latest allegation.

articles.title: Mexico cancels plans to end school year early for World Cup
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico's government has reversed its decision to end the school year early due to concerns raised by parents and education experts. The original plan, announced in May, aimed to ease traffic during the Fifa World Cup and a heatwave.  After backlash from the National Union of Parents, President Claudia Sheinbaum clarified that ending classes early was only a proposal. The decision has been scrapped, with classes now scheduled to finish on July 15th.

articles.title: NEET-UG 2026 cancelled LIVE: CBI to probe paper leak allegations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 exam held on May 3rd after allegations of a paper leak. The decision follows investigations by both the Rajasthan Special Operations Group and the CBI, with the government approving the cancellation to ensure transparency.  The examination will be re-conducted at a later date, details of which will be announced separately.

articles.title: NSUI protests after NTA cancels NEET-UG 2026 over paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A massive protest organized by the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) erupted outside the Shastri Bhawan on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, demanding justice for students alleging a paper leak in the NEET-UG exam.  The protest saw members of the Congress party's student wing participate, holding signs and slogans criticizing the government's handling of the situation. The National Testing Agency (NTA) canceled the examination following investigations by the Rajasthan Special Operations Group (SOG) and the CBI.  The NSUI accused the central government of failing to protect students and demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a ban on the NTA.

articles.title: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy meets Governor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy invited Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to a program on June 12th, celebrating the reopening of schools. The program will feature the administration of a mass pledge against tobacco, alcohol, and drugs, along with the distribution of educational kits containing uniforms, textbooks, notebooks, school bags, sportswear, and other study materials.

articles.title: Birmingham City University urged not to axe Black studies MA | Higher education | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 100 academics, writers, and activists have signed an open letter condemning the closure of Birmingham City University’s (BCU) MA in Black studies and global justice.  The move follows the controversial closure of BCU's undergraduate Black studies course in 2024, prompting concerns about the erasure of Black studies from UK higher education. Prof Kehinde Andrews, a leading commentator who pioneered the development of BCU’s Black studies program, has called for the decision to be reviewed, citing potential discrimination and the university's failure to consult staff or students.  The university blames low recruitment but acknowledges that current students will be able to complete their studies.

articles.title: DME panel completes inquiry into mental harassment charges at Kozhikode medical college - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A three-member panel appointed by the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) has completed its inquiry into allegations of mental harassment against two faculty members at the Department of Psychiatry, Government Medical College, Kozhikode. The panel is expected to submit a report soon.  The members include Varghese P. Punnoos, Principal, Government Medical College, Kottayam, P.S. Indu, Principal, Government Medical College, Thrissur, and C. Raveendran, secretary of the Institutional Ethics Committee, Government Medical College, Thrissur.

articles.title: 3-month-long summer vacation announced for Punjab schools - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rana Sikandar Hayat, Punjab Education Minister, announced a three-month summer vacation for schools in the province, beginning May 22 and ending August 23.  The decision follows previous advisories from the Punjab Disaster Management Authority urging schools to adjust working hours or declare early summer holidays due to excessive heat. The authority's directives included measures such as altering working hours, suspending outdoor activities, ensuring water availability, maintaining ventilation systems, and advising students to wear light-colored clothing.

articles.title: Education Budget will grow every year, says Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced that the Telangana government will prioritize education, aiming for a 15% allocation in future budgets, gradually increasing from the current 7.6%.  He highlighted the implementation of several initiatives since December 2023, including teacher recruitment, DSC notifications, and global exchange programs. The "Exclusive Education Week" celebrations aim to showcase progress and improve learning facilities across the state. Mr. Reddy emphasized that education is an investment in the future and stressed the importance of teachers in building a better society.

articles.title: Telangana BIE re-releases admission schedule; classes for Inter first year to begin from June 1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Board of Intermediate Education (BIE) released the admissions schedule for 2026-27, with phase-I admissions starting on Tuesday and concluding by June 30.  Principals are instructed to make provisional admissions based on internet marks memo downloaded by candidates, which will be confirmed upon presentation of original SSC pass certificates and transfer certificates. The BIE also mandated Aadhaar details for students and directed colleges to limit sections to a maximum of 88 students with prior approval for additional sections.

articles.title: Summit highlights urgency of aligning education with future job markets - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo University, Chittoor and the University of Leicester jointly hosted the second edition of the Apollo-Leicester Education Summit-2026 in Vijayawada. The summit brought together diplomats, academic leaders, and industry experts from both countries to discuss how students can prepare for careers in 2030 and beyond.  Daniel Ladley, Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University of Leicester School of Business, emphasized the importance of globally relevant, employability-focused education. Gareth Wynn Owen, British Deputy High Commissioner for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, highlighted the growing collaboration between India and the UK in education, innovation, and careers.

articles.title: HEC launches online degree attestation system to facilitate students - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Higher Education Commission of Pakistan (HEC) launched a fully online and paperless degree attestation system to streamline the process for students.  Dr Niaz Ahmed Akhtar, HEC Chairman, announced that applicants will no longer need to visit HEC offices or submit original documents. The new system allows for 24/7 application submission through the HEC e-Services Portal.  Applicants can upload transcripts and pay online, with an e-certificate issued upon final review.

articles.title: Why a ministerial vacancy nearly delayed Class 12 Board exam results in T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The School Education Department of Tamil Nadu postponed the release date for Class 12 State Board exam results due to a lack of a Minister to authorize the announcement. This decision caused significant disappointment among students, teachers, and parents as it disrupted their preparation plans.  After facing backlash from various stakeholders, including child rights groups and educationists, the department reversed its decision and released the results on May 8th, as scheduled. Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar urged the department to release the scores without delay.

articles.title: A.P. EAPCET-2026 to begin from May 12 across A.P. and Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) has completed preparations for the A.P. EAPCET-2026, a common entrance test for engineering, agriculture, and pharmacy programs, scheduled for May 12-20 in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.  B. Tirupati Rao, Council Secretary, announced that over 355,000 candidates applied online this year. The exam will be computer-based with two sessions: 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 2 p.m. to 5 p.m., overseen by Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University (JNTU)-Kakinada and chaired by N. Mohan Rao.

articles.title: From flight journey to land gifts, SSC toppers receive unique rewards in A.P. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students in Andhra Pradesh are being recognized for their academic achievement in the SSC Public Examinations-2026.  In Vizianagaram district, A. Hemanth, the school topper with 581 marks, was given a flight experience from Visakhapatnam to Vijayawada by his lab assistant, Miriyala Krishna Rao. The gesture aims to provide students with both academic success and memorable life experiences.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: “Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Aristotle's famous quote, "Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all," highlights the importance of emotional intelligence alongside academic achievement.  The quote emphasizes that true education should develop both intellectual and compassionate qualities for individuals to contribute positively to society.  Modern educators are increasingly recognizing the need to incorporate emotional learning into educational systems as students face increasing pressures to succeed academically while also grappling with mental health challenges like anxiety, burnout, and loneliness.  This shift in focus reflects a growing understanding that emotional intelligence is crucial for leadership, teamwork, communication, and overall well-being.

articles.title: Around 1,10,787 candidates attended COMED-K UGET - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 110,787 candidates took the COMED-K UGET entrance exam across India, with approximately 35,678 in Karnataka. The exam, a gateway to admissions into 20,000 seats at engineering colleges in the state, was held in two sessions on Saturday.  The provisional answer keys will be released on May 13th and the final key on May 20th. Students can access their rank cards on May 26th.

articles.title: Teacher dies of heart attack while giving lecture-cum-demonstration at training session in Khammam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Jayaraj, an English teacher at a private school in Khammam, died of a heart attack during a training workshop on Saturday. The incident occurred while he was conducting the workshop for teachers in Khammam district.  He was declared brought dead at a local hospital after being rushed there. Jayaraj was considered an expert in teachers' training and his colleagues are mourning his sudden passing.

articles.title: Grant EL to teachers handling SSC remedial classes: FAPTO - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: FAPTO members have requested the School Education Department to grant Earned Leave (EL) to teachers conducting special and remedial classes for SSC failed students during the summer vacation. The request was made in a representation submitted to Director of School Education Thameem Ansariya, who issued orders for these classes following the 2026 SSC exams.

articles.title: SPCSS-TN calls Centre’s higher education bill unconstitutional, demands its withdrawal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Platform for Common School System – Tamil Nadu (SPCSS-TN) has written to the Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill 2025, arguing it is unconstitutional and should be withdrawn. The letter claims the bill grants excessive power to the Union government, potentially leading to the privatization of education and undermining state universities' role in social justice.  The SPCSS-TN also criticizes the bill for failing to recognize the importance of state universities in India's development and for its potential to create a subservient educational system.

articles.title: Mexican parents criticise ending school year a month early for World Cup
articles.rephrased_article: Mexican parents and organizations have criticized the Mexican government's proposal to end the school year a month early for the World Cup. The decision, citing increased travel and heatwaves, was met with anger from parents who expressed concerns about childcare arrangements and economic impacts.  The National Union of Parents condemned the plan as "unilateral" and called it "inexcusable." Business owners also criticized the sudden change, calling for individual states to address the disruption. Despite initial support from some state governments, President Claudia Sheinbaum has since softened her stance, stating that the proposal is under review.

articles.title: Oldest Forest school in Jawadhu Hills secures 98% in Plus Two examinations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Forest Department schools in Tamil Nadu achieved high pass rates in the 2026 Plus Two examinations. The Forest Government Higher Secondary School in Pudur Nadu, a tribal village in Jawadhu Hills of Tirupattur district, topped the list with a 98% pass percentage, exceeding other forest schools in Jamunamarathur and Nellivasal which achieved 97% and 93% respectively.

articles.title: The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling 2026 turns into informative session on career choices - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Nasir Mauzam, a career counsellor from CIGMA, spoke at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling 2026 in Bidar, encouraging students to explore diverse career options beyond traditional paths. He emphasized the importance of self-reflection and informed decision-making, highlighting the vast array of professions available.  Sachin Gudge, an associate professor at Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences, discussed the demanding nature of medicine but also its rewarding aspects. Parvat Bijaspur, a chartered accountant, spoke about the lucrative career opportunities in commerce, while Vinita Balbhim Patil, principal of Lingaraj Appa College of Engineering, stressed the enduring relevance of engineering despite technological advancements.  Ramesh Kulkarni, chairman of Sri Mata Manikeshwari PU College, urged students to prioritize character development and avoid social media addiction. Dayanand J., CET nodal officer, provided guidance on choosing colleges based on individual merit and ranking.

articles.title: Beyond the textbook - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's education system is facing criticism for its focus on rote learning, but a growing movement advocates for incorporating hands-on coding and robotics into the curriculum.  This approach, known as "active learning," allows students to experience concepts firsthand, bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application. By engaging with technology like microcontrollers and sensors, students learn physics, mathematics, and logic through real-world projects. This not only builds problem-solving skills but also fosters empathy and a sense of social responsibility.  Integrating robotics into education can empower students to become creators and innovators, preparing them for the demands of a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

articles.title: BC hostels emerge as top-performing welfare hostels in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Backward Classes Welfare Hostels in Andhra Pradesh have achieved the highest satisfaction rate among welfare hostels, according to a parent feedback survey conducted by the government. The Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) revealed a 78.20% satisfaction rate for these hostels, surpassing other categories. S. Savitha, the BC Welfare Minister, attributes this improvement to the government's focus on strengthening educational support, infrastructure, nutrition, and student welfare.

articles.title: EAPCET 2026 engineering test records 93% attendance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Council of Higher Education Chairman V. Balakista Reddy, JNTUH Vice-Chancellor T. Kishen Kumar Reddy, and TG EAPCET Convener K. Vijaya Kumar Reddy witnessed high attendance rates for the engineering stream of the 2026 EAPCET, with 93.44% and 93.05% participation in the first and second sessions respectively. The highest attendance was recorded in districts like Nalgonda, Nizamabad, Karimnagar, and Bhadradri Kothagudem, with over 32,000 candidates attending each session out of a total of 34,823 allotted for the morning session.

articles.title: Bidar: Take informed decisions about career paths, IAS officer tells students at The Hindu EducationPlus Career Counselling 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Shinde, a senior IAS officer and Belagavi Zilla Panchayat CEO, advised students to choose rewarding careers while developing resilience. He emphasized focusing on personal interests and aptitude rather than fleeting trends or job market demands. Dayananda J., CET nodal officer, provided details about the KEA CET examination and counselling.  Sachin Gudge, associate professor at Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences, spoke about medicine as a career path. Other speakers included Vinita Balbhim Patil, principal of Lingaraj Appa Engineering College, and Parvat Bijaspur, CA, who discussed careers in commerce.

articles.title: Uae Education: UAE to decide on remote or in-person classes on May 10 as schools and universities remain on alert | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UAE schools, universities, and nurseries are awaiting a decision on May 10th regarding the future of their learning model. The Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, and Dubai’s Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) will announce the new model after completing a nationwide safety assessment.  The decision prioritizes student and staff safety while ensuring education continuity.

articles.title: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education declares Class X exam results; 86.83% students pass - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Board of Secondary Education announced the Class X results, with 86.83% of the total 9.71 lakh candidates passing. Ramanuj Ganguly, president of the board, stated that this year's pass rate was similar to last year's at 86.56%.  Abhirup Bhadra from Uttar Dinajpur secured the top rank with 698 out of 700 marks, while Priyotosh Mukhopadhyay from Birbhum placed second. The third rank was shared by three students. Kalimpong recorded the highest pass rate at 95.01%, followed by Purba Medinipur and Kolkata.

articles.title: 60 centres get ready for Inter supplementary exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam Joint Collector Gobbilla Vidyadhari directed officials to ensure smooth and error-free Intermediate Advanced Supplementary examinations from May 21st to June 2nd. The examinations will be held in 60 centers across the district, with first year exams running from 9 a.m. to 12 noon and second year exams from 2:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.

articles.title: Prisons report 98.33% pass in Class 12 State board exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's Department of Prisons and Correctional Services reported a 98.33% pass rate in the Class XII board examinations, with all three top scorers being prisoners at the Central Prison, Palayamkottai.  The Tamil Nadu School Education Department established examination centers within prisons based on requests from prison officials. The top three scorers were P. Vinith (549 marks), T. Manikandan (531 marks), and B. Balu (527 marks).

articles.title: Sexual harassment more than twice as prevalent at England’s top universities, analysis finds | Students | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A national survey of undergraduates revealed that students at high tariff universities, those requiring the highest A-level grades for entry, were more than twice as likely to experience sexual harassment compared to those at lower tariff institutions.  The analysis by the Office for Students, England's higher education regulator, found hotspots of sexual harassment and violence in courses like medicine, dentistry, veterinary sciences or languages. Jo Grady, general secretary of the University and College Union, expressed concern that perpetrators from these prestigious universities could perpetuate toxic cultures while Prof Libby Hackett, chief executive of the Russell Group, acknowledged the need for continued efforts to ensure student safety on campus.

articles.title: Class 12 State Board exams: Tamil Nadu registers 95.2% pass rate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Class 12 State Board examination results showed a marginal increase in pass percentage to 95.2%, with Erode district achieving the highest rate of 98.8%.  A total of 7,91,654 students sat for the exams, with girls outperforming boys at 97% compared to 93.19% for boys. School Education Secretary B. Chandra Mohan announced provisional certificates will be available from May 13th and supplementary exams for Class 12 will begin on June 29th.  The outgoing Chief Minister, M.K. Stalin, congratulated the students and urged them to pursue higher education.

articles.title: Maharashtra Class 10 results out; over 92% students pass, girls outperform boys again - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) announced the Class 10 results, with an overall pass percentage of 92.09%. Girls performed better than boys, achieving a 94.96% pass rate compared to boys' 89.56%. The Kokan division topped the list with 97.62%, while the Chatrapati Sambhajinagar division recorded the lowest pass percentage at 88.41%.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exam results: How to check? - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exam results
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Government Examinations, Tamil Nadu, announced the Class 12 examination results on May 8, 2026. Students can access their results online through tnresults.nic.in and dge.tn.gov.in.  They can also check their results via WhatsApp by saving the number +91-7845252525 and sending a "Hi" message with their registration number and date of birth. Additionally, students can download their marksheets through DigiLocker by following specific steps outlined in the article.

articles.title: 4 children killed, 20 people injured as roof of classroom collapses in Dera Ghazi Khan school - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: At least four children and 20 others were injured when the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan, Punjab, collapsed on Thursday. The incident occurred around noon, prompting a rescue operation involving Rescue 1122, district administration officials, and local residents.  The preliminary report attributed the collapse to an overloaded roof due to construction work being carried out during school hours. District Education Authority CEO Waqas Gill assured that the incident would be investigated and action taken against the school administration. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has also taken notice of the incident.

articles.title: Cambridge to retake ‘prematurely shared’ AS-level mathematics exam on June 9 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) canceled the AS-level mathematics exam for affected regions due to a premature release of the paper. The organization will administer a new version of the exam on June 9th, ensuring fair outcomes and grades trusted by universities. CIE stated that no additional charge will be incurred by candidates or schools, and the result date remains August 11th.  The examination body is investigating the leak and has emphasized its commitment to upholding ethical standards and protecting student integrity.

articles.title: Cusat steps up initiatives to help students deal with mental stress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the back-to-back suicides of engineering students at Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat), the university has announced a multi-pronged approach to address mental health concerns.  The plan includes increased counselling support, improved teacher-student interactions, and confidence-building programs for students. The university will also convene regular meetings with parents and teachers to inform them about these initiatives. Cusat officials emphasized their commitment to improving student well-being by providing all-round support from faculty members and the administration.

articles.title: Sindh to provide cash assistance to caregivers of children up to five - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah chaired the third board meeting of the Sindh Social Protection Authority (SSPA), approving a Rs14 billion Early Childhood Development (ECD) program. The initiative will provide quarterly payments of Rs3,000 to over 885,000 children aged one month to five years old for growth monitoring, nutrition counseling, and school readiness.  The meeting also approved upgrades to the Mamta maternal health cash transfer program and a new Women Agricultural Workers Programme to provide seasonal income assistance to rural women. The government aims to strengthen long-term human development through these programs.

articles.title: 18 Russian medical varsities to take part in education fair - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Russian universities will participate in an All India Russian Education Fair across Tamil Nadu this month, offering 10,000 MBBS seats to Indian students. The fair is open to those who have cleared the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test and scored at least 50% marks in relevant core subjects. Russian Consul General Valerii Khodzhaev stated that Russia aims to attract 5,00,000 foreign students by 2030. The fair will be held across several cities in Tamil Nadu from May 9th to 14th and offers full scholarships to about 220 Indian students.

articles.title: Overseas scholarship forAdi Dravidar, tribal students - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department
articles.rephrased_article: The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department has announced the application period for scholarships under the Annal Ambedkar Overseas Higher Education Scholarship Scheme, open to students from the Adi Dravidar community, Adi Dravidar converts to Christianity, and tribal communities.  Applicants must have been admitted to a Master's or PhD program at a foreign university ranked within the top 1000 by QS World University Rankings and have an annual family income of no more than ₹12 lakh. The deadline for applications is June 5, 2026. Eligible candidates can apply online through the department's website between May 5 and June 5.

articles.title: Online process to join arts and science colleges begins today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students seeking admission to first-year undergraduate degree programs in government arts and science colleges in the state for the 2026-27 academic year can register online starting May 7th. The application fee is ₹48, with a waiver for students from SC and ST communities.  The last day for registration is May 29th. Students can find more information on the website www.tngasa.in or contact the Directorate of Collegiate Education help center at 044-24343100 and 24342011 between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. weekdays.

articles.title: UCLA medical school illegally used race in admissions, justice department finds | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice found that the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA illegally considered race in admissions, escalating a standoff with the university over allegations of antisemitism. The department cited data showing admitted Black and Hispanic students had lower average grade-point averages and test scores compared to their white and Asian American counterparts.  The findings come as part of ongoing investigations into possible race-based discrimination in medical school admissions at other institutions, including Stanford, Ohio State, and the University of California, San Diego. The department also took issue with an application document that invited students to disclose their membership in marginalized groups.

articles.title: Singapore introduces caning for boys who bully others at school | Singapore | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Singapore's education minister, Desmond Lee, announced new guidelines that will allow male students in upper primary levels (age 9-12 years) and above to face caning as a last resort for bullying. Unicef, the UN’s agency for children, opposes corporal punishment, arguing it harms children's physical and mental health.  Lee emphasized that caning would only be used after other measures have failed and will be administered under strict protocols by authorized teachers. Schools will monitor student well-being and provide counseling following the punishment.

articles.title: Maharashtra to upgrade 19 secondary ashram schools to junior college for tribals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra government approved upgrading 19 secondary schools and 5 primary ashram schools to higher levels under the Tribal Development Department.  This decision aims to prevent dropouts and improve educational progress for tribal students in remote areas. The upgrades will create new positions and funding for these schools, which currently serve over 2.6 million students across the state.  The Maharashtra government's decision is part of a larger effort to provide quality education to all students, particularly those from marginalized communities.

articles.title: Student–faculty ratio at SSUS under scrutiny - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS)'s low student-to-high faculty ratio has been flagged as financially unsustainable. A Syndicate sub-committee assessment revealed a teacher-student ratio significantly below the recommended range, ranging from 1:15 to 1:20. The report highlighted disparities across regional campuses with varying ratios, including 1:3.75 at Ettumanoor, 1:4.59 at Thiruvananthapuram, and 1:6.42 at Panmana.  The committee concluded that the university's current faculty strength of 303 would require a higher student headcount to justify expenses.

articles.title: ‘In learning organisations, failure is not a bad word’ - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
articles.rephrased_article: SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) and The Hindu hosted a panel discussion on "The Future Reimagined – Discover, Decide, Define Your Career" where speakers emphasized the importance of learning organizations for employee success.  Speakers highlighted that organizations that invest in employee upskilling and reskilling are more likely to thrive. They stressed the need for a culture that embraces failure as a learning opportunity and rewards employees for their efforts to develop new skills. Amardeep Devadasan, Senior Vice-President, RR Donnelley & Williams Lea, echoed this sentiment, emphasizing that learning should be a pull rather than a push.  Bijumon Jacob, Head-India Operations, Human Resources, Ejada, Dubai, also emphasized the importance of fostering a mindset shift within employees to embrace continuous learning and development.

articles.title: France serves up €1 meals to all university students in effort to cut hardship | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: French universities have begun offering a €1 meal to all students, down from the usual €3.30, in an effort to address financial hardship. The policy is aimed at alleviating financial strain for students who are struggling to afford food. The government has pledged €120 million in 2027 to support the program, which saw a 5.3% increase in beneficiaries in 2024.

articles.title: Uae School Break: UAE announces 9-day Eid Al Adha school break starting May 25 for students across private and public schools | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UAE schools are adjusting their schedules to accommodate the extended Eid Al Adha holiday period, which is expected to merge with the mid-term break. The UAE Ministry of Education has confirmed a separate mid-term break from May 25 to May 29, potentially resulting in a nine-day holiday for students.  Private schools are reorganizing academic schedules to ensure consistency and prevent students from falling behind while also acknowledging the importance of family time during Eid celebrations. Educators are using digital learning platforms to maintain student engagement during the break. The extended holiday period is expected to lead to increased travel demand across the UAE, with families planning trips and visits.

articles.title: BSEK chairman resigns following allegations of mismanagement of matric exams in Karachi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ghulam Hussain Soho, chairman of the Board of Secondary Education Karachi (BSEK), resigned following a committee report recommending his suspension due to irregularities and mismanagement during the ongoing matric examinations. The report revealed that Soho made changes to 170 examination centres without authorization, prompting the resignation.  The BSEK affirmed its commitment to strengthening the educational system despite the challenges faced.

articles.title: ‘My goal was not immigration’: Oxford law graduate on why she’s returning to India from UK - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Niyati, an Indian student who graduated from University of Oxford with a law degree, has decided to return home after two months. She stated that her decision was driven by a commitment to Pratisandhi, an initiative she is deeply invested in, and the desire to contribute to its growth. While acknowledging uncertainty about the future, Niyati emphasized prioritizing long-term fulfillment over conventional definitions of success.

articles.title: POLYCET 2026: 91.37% pass in Andhra Pradesh; girls outdo boys, ASR district tops list - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A total of 1,48,950 candidates qualified for diploma courses in Andhra Pradesh after the POLYCET 2026 recorded a pass percentage of 91.37%.  The high turnout, exceeding 23,000 students compared to last year, saw girls outperform boys with a pass percentage of 93.57% against 89.88%. The SBTET attributed the strong performance to better access to technical education in remote areas.  Nara Lokesh, the Human Resource Development Minister, commended the students' success and encouraged those who did not qualify to remain determined.

articles.title: In Mauritania, push to phase out private schools divides opinion | Education | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mauritania's government is phasing out private schools in favor of state-run institutions to improve education quality and address systemic discrimination. While the move aims to standardize education and make it more accessible, critics warn that the rapid implementation will lead to job losses and lower education standards. The policy has sparked protests from private school owners, teachers, and parents who fear financial hardship and reduced educational opportunities. Moulay Ould Rais, a retired engineer and parent, supports the government's initiative, believing it will bring about unity and equality in education.  However, some argue that the focus on unifying children through public schools ignores existing social divisions within Mauritania. The government emphasizes its efforts to level the playing field for all Mauritanian children, regardless of their background or language.

articles.title: One in four humanities students in Australia to take more than 25 years to pay off student loans, treasury finds | Australian universities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Treasury modeling reveals that the Morrison government's job ready graduates (JRG) program, introduced in 2021, has significantly increased student debt for humanities and creative arts students. The program, designed to incentivize study in science, nursing, education, and IT fields, will leave almost two-thirds of these students with debts exceeding $50,000, with median repayment times increasing from 14 to 17 years.  Independent senator David Pocock has called for urgent reform, while Education Minister Jason Clare has acknowledged the program's failure in its intended goal and stated that the government is taking steps towards reform. Western Sydney University vice-chancellor George Williams highlighted the need for policy changes and a timetable for addressing the issue of long-term student debt.
